status: PROPOSAL (research/2026-10-07, pattern-mining agent). Not part of schema/entry.schema.json; nothing in the dataset depends on it.
purpose: A controlled vocabulary for a possible future per-algorithm 'technique' field, plus a draft mapping of every entry that had an entry.json when this file was written.

how_to_read.techniques: Each technique has an id, a name, a definition (what the algorithm does) and the structural property of the problem it exploits.
how_to_read.baselines: Kinds of SLOW algorithm. A baseline is a description of the slow side, not a technique.
how_to_read.mapping.algorithms: One record per algorithm of the entry, in the entry's order and with the entry's exact name: role (slow / intermediate / fast / peer), baseline kind (slow side only), techniques used.
how_to_read.mapping.transformation: The technique(s) that turn the slowest algorithm into the fastest one: the pair-level pattern used for the taxonomy.
how_to_read.mapping.domain: Coarse problem domain, assigned by the mapper (used only for gap statistics).
how_to_read.mapping.confidence: high = the entry's own text states the mechanism; medium = staging entry or a judgement call by the mapper.
how_to_read.mapping.provisional: true = entry added by a parallel agent during the 2026-10-07 session; its text may still change.

techniques.name: Memoisation / dynamic programming
techniques.definition: Solve each distinct subproblem once, store the answer, and combine stored answers with a recurrence (a Bellman equation).
techniques.exploited_property: Optimal substructure plus a set of distinct subproblems far smaller than the recursion tree or the solution space (polynomial for the T2 cases in this dataset).

techniques.name: Dynamic programming over subsets
techniques.definition: A dynamic program whose state is a subset of the ground set together with O(1) boundary information (e.g. the last element).
techniques.exploited_property: The value of a partial solution depends on WHICH elements it uses, not on their order, so n!-type enumeration collapses to 2^n poly(n) or 3^n states.

techniques.name: Divide and conquer (combinatorial)
techniques.definition: Split the instance into independent parts, solve them recursively, and combine the answers in (near-)linear time.
techniques.exploited_property: The answer decomposes over a partition with a cheap merge step (sorted halves, the strip lemma, cross inversions).

techniques.name: Bilinear algebraic recursion (tensor-rank amplification)
techniques.definition: Use a fixed-size bilinear identity with fewer multiplications than the definition, and apply it recursively to blocks.
techniques.exploited_property: The problem is a bilinear map over a ring whose fixed-format tensor rank r is below the naive count; a format-k scheme of rank r gives exponent log_k r (for square formats).

techniques.name: Fast algebraic transform (FFT / NTT / Walsh-Hadamard / zeta-Moebius)
techniques.definition: Change to a basis in which the operation is pointwise, using a recursively factorised transform.
techniques.exploited_property: The operation (cyclic, XOR or subset convolution) is diagonalised by the characters of a group or by the zeta/Moebius pair of the subset lattice, and the transform factorises into O(log N) sparse stages.

techniques.name: Elimination preserving an algebraic invariant
techniques.definition: Apply elementary operations that preserve (or change predictably) the quantity sought, until it can be read off a triangular form.
techniques.exploited_property: Invariance of the target (determinant, rank, solution space) under row operations; this is exactly what the permanent lacks.

techniques.name: Inclusion-exclusion
techniques.definition: Replace a sum over constrained structures by an alternating sum, over subsets, of unconstrained counts restricted to each subset.
techniques.exploited_property: The constraint is of 'covering' type (every element used: permutations, covers, partitions), and unconstrained counts restricted to a subset are cheap.

techniques.name: Meet in the middle
techniques.definition: Split the variables into two halves, enumerate each half, and combine the halves by sorting or hashing.
techniques.exploited_property: The objective/constraint is additive across the split, so combining reduces to a one-dimensional search (binary search, hash lookup).

techniques.name: Greedy choice justified by an exchange or cut argument
techniques.definition: Make the locally best choice at every step; an exchange argument, cut property or label-setting argument proves it is never wrong.
techniques.exploited_property: Matroid / cut structure (MST), or monotonicity of labels under non-negative weights (Dijkstra), or an exchange-sortable objective (scheduling rules).

techniques.name: LP duality / potentials
techniques.definition: Maintain dual variables (potentials) that certify optimality and reweight costs so that cheap subroutines (e.g. Dijkstra) apply.
techniques.exploited_property: The problem is a linear program with integral optimal vertices or a min-max theorem (assignment, flows).

techniques.name: Augmenting paths in a residual structure
techniques.definition: Improve a feasible solution along an improving path in a residual graph; choose paths (e.g. shortest) so that few rounds suffice.
techniques.exploited_property: A solution is optimal iff no improving path exists (flow / matching optimality conditions).

techniques.name: Phased augmentation along shortest paths (blocking flows)
techniques.definition: In each phase, compute residual distances once (BFS) and augment along a maximal set of shortest augmenting paths, so the shortest-path length strictly grows from phase to phase.
techniques.exploited_property: Monotonicity of residual s-t distances; few phases suffice (O(sqrt V) for matching, at most V - 1 for flow).

techniques.name: Amortised single scan
techniques.definition: Scan the input once, reusing information about already-processed overlaps so that the total work is linear by an amortisation argument.
techniques.exploited_property: Self-similarity of the structure being matched: borders of the pattern (KMP), mirror symmetry of palindromes (Manacher).

techniques.name: Finite-automaton compilation or simulation
techniques.definition: Compile the pattern(s) into a finite automaton, or simulate a nondeterministic automaton with a set of states, so the text is read once.
techniques.exploited_property: The language to recognise is regular (or a finite union of patterns), so the relevant state after a prefix is finite and independent of how the prefix was matched.

techniques.name: Incremental reuse of the previous result
techniques.definition: Obtain the next quantity from the previous one in O(1) instead of recomputing it from scratch.
techniques.exploited_property: Quantities for nested or overlapping ranges are additive or nested (running sums; palindromes sharing a center).

techniques.name: Sort, then exploit monotonicity
techniques.definition: Sort once, then answer the question by a monotone scan: two pointers, binary search, or comparison of neighbours.
techniques.exploited_property: After sorting, the relevant predicate is monotone in the index (pair sums, LIS tails), or equal items become adjacent.

techniques.name: Specialised data structure
techniques.definition: Answer the repeated inner query with a structure built for it (union-find, heaps, sparse tables, Fenwick trees, suffix automata).
techniques.exploited_property: The inner query has exploitable algebra: disjoint-set merges, associativity or idempotence of the combining operation, a total order.

techniques.name: Doubling / exponentiation by squaring
techniques.definition: Compute x^e with O(log e) operations by squaring and multiplying along the bits of e.
techniques.exploited_property: Associativity of a monoid operation (modular multiplication, matrix product, function composition).

techniques.name: Invariant-preserving reduction (Euclidean descent)
techniques.definition: Replace the instance by a strictly smaller one with the same answer, so the size shrinks geometrically.
techniques.exploited_property: An identity such as gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b) together with a guaranteed size decrease (Lame's bound).

techniques.name: Algebraic characterisation checked in a small ring
techniques.definition: Decide the property by checking a polynomial identity that is equivalent to it, modulo a small ideal.
techniques.exploited_property: (X + a)^N = X^N + a (mod N) characterises primes; working modulo (X^r - 1, N) keeps the check polynomial.

techniques.name: Randomisation with abundant witnesses
techniques.definition: Sample random certificates; if a constant fraction of samples are witnesses, a few samples decide with one-sided error.
techniques.exploited_property: Witness abundance: >= 3/4 of bases for Miller-Rabin, Schwartz-Zippel for polynomial identities, half of all points for balanced functions.

techniques.name: Birthday-paradox collision search
techniques.definition: Sample random points until two collide; a hidden pairing or period is then revealed.
techniques.exploited_property: A hidden 2-to-1 structure or period makes collisions appear after about sqrt(N) samples.

techniques.name: Estimation from random samples
techniques.definition: Estimate an average, correlation or acceptance probability from independent random samples, with Chernoff/Hoeffding error bounds.
techniques.exploited_property: The quantity is an expectation of a bounded random variable, so O(1/eps^2) samples give additive error eps.

techniques.name: Randomised processing order
techniques.definition: Process items in random order (random pivots, random child order, random incremental construction) to defeat worst-case inputs.
techniques.exploited_property: Expected work averaged over the algorithm's own coin flips is small for EVERY input (backward analysis; recursive hedging).

techniques.name: Randomised local search / random restarts
techniques.definition: Random initial assignment plus a short random walk or random-order forced assignment, restarted many times.
techniques.exploited_property: From a random start, a solution is reached with probability exponentially larger than 2^-n (Schoening, PPSZ).

techniques.name: Branching with reduction rules (measure-and-conquer analysis)
techniques.definition: Recursive branching on local configurations, with polynomial-time reduction rules; the branching vectors give a recurrence whose dominant root bounds the running time.
techniques.exploited_property: Local structure (degree, neighbourhood) forces large size reductions in every branch.

techniques.name: Monotone / Monge matrix search (DP speed-ups)
techniques.definition: Exploit monotonicity of optimal split points or row minima (Knuth-Yao quadrangle inequality, SMAWK, divide-and-conquer optimisation).
techniques.exploited_property: Totally monotone or Monge cost matrices; quadrangle inequalities on DP weights.

techniques.name: Counting via determinants (matrix-tree, Pfaffians)
techniques.definition: Express a count of combinatorial structures as a determinant or Pfaffian, then compute it by elimination.
techniques.exploited_property: A sign-reversing structure makes unwanted terms cancel (Kirchhoff's matrix-tree theorem, Kasteleyn orientations for planar graphs).

techniques.name: Structured / Krylov linear algebra
techniques.definition: Exploit matrix structure (band, Toeplitz, sparsity) or Krylov sequences and minimal polynomials (Levinson, Thomas, Wiedemann, Berlekamp-Massey).
techniques.exploited_property: Low displacement rank, bandedness, or cheap matrix-vector products.

techniques.name: Quantum interference / Fourier sampling
techniques.definition: Prepare a superposition, query the oracle in phase or in a second register, apply a (quantum) Fourier transform and measure.
techniques.exploited_property: The hidden object (linear function, period, hidden subgroup, constant-vs-balanced) is a character or coset structure of an abelian group.

techniques.name: Amplitude amplification
techniques.definition: Alternate a phase oracle with a reflection about the start state to rotate amplitude toward marked states.
techniques.exploited_property: A checkable predicate; success amplitude grows linearly in the number of iterations, so probability grows quadratically faster than classical repetition.

techniques.name: Quantum walk
techniques.definition: Replace a classical random walk on a graph by a quantum walk (search on Johnson graphs, glued trees).
techniques.exploited_property: Spectral gap and marked-set structure of the walk graph.

techniques.name: Quantum linear algebra (phase estimation on encoded matrices)
techniques.definition: Phase estimation / singular value transformation on a matrix given by QRAM or block encoding.
techniques.exploited_property: Low rank or well-conditioned matrices with efficient state preparation; the speedup depends on the input model.

techniques.name: Length-squared (l2) sampling (dequantisation)
techniques.definition: Sample rows/entries with probability proportional to squared norms to simulate the state preparation a quantum algorithm assumes.
techniques.exploited_property: Low-rank structure plus sample-and-query access comparable to QRAM.

techniques.name: Group-theoretic divide and conquer
techniques.definition: Use permutation-group algorithms and structure theory to prune the space of isomorphisms.
techniques.exploited_property: Automorphism-group structure (Luks; Babai's local certificates).

techniques.name: Sieving and smoothness (index calculus)
techniques.definition: Collect relations among smooth numbers in suitable rings, then combine them by linear algebra.
techniques.exploited_property: Density of smooth numbers (heuristic L-notation estimates).

techniques.name: Continuous optimisation (ellipsoid, interior point)
techniques.definition: Follow a central path or shrink an ellipsoid in the continuous relaxation; round at the end.
techniques.exploited_property: Convexity of the feasible region; polynomially bounded bit sizes (weakly polynomial bounds).

techniques.name: Preflow-push (push-relabel)
techniques.definition: Maintain a preflow and vertex labels; push excess along admissible edges and relabel when stuck.
techniques.exploited_property: Distance labels bound the number of relabels and saturating pushes.

Transcribe a recurrence directly; overlapping subproblems are recomputed.
Loop over a range proportional to the numeric VALUE of an input number; exponential in its bit length.
Evaluate the defining formula term by term (schoolbook product, convolution).
A simpler polynomial algorithm that repeats work (insertion sort, running sums, expand-around-centers).
Run an algorithm for a simpler problem many times (Bellman-Ford from every source).
Classical query algorithm used as the baseline of a quantum query separation (T9).
A serious classical algorithm that is the best known for an open (T6) or dequantised (T5) problem.
The quantum algorithm whose claimed advantage a T5 entry dequantises.
